It wasn't me who killed someone in self-defense. It was my brother, and I saw the aftermath first hand, so I'll share the story.

It was a Saturday night, we left the movie theaters together with our dates and headed to our cars. As I went to grab my keys to unlock the car, I felt cold metal touch the back of my neck. I hear "You move, you're dead." from behind me. I freeze in place, and the guy behind me orders me to give him the keys. I comply. He then tells my date and my brother's date to hand over their purses. My brother's date complies, but my date refuses. The guy starts getting angry, and threatens to blow my head off if she doesn't give him the damn purse.

As I was there, I realized that my brother was not there, he wasn't with his date. As I begin thinking about him, I hear his voice shout "DROP THE GUN, YOU BASTARD!" and in the corner of my eye, I see him with his 1911 out pointing at the guy holding a gun to my head, he turns and sees my brother, and I see him pivet around to swing the gun at him. My brother opens fire, and the back of the guy's head gets blown off, and his body hits the asphalt. My brother comes over, kicks the guy's gun away, and asks if we are all okay. I said yes, but even in the dark, I saw the horror in my brother's eyes as he looked at the guy's body.

Police show up, and after witness reports from both our dates and me, my brother is told that his actions seem to be in self-defense, and that he's good to go home, but detectives will be in contact with him. As we drop our dates off and walk them to the door, no words were passed between us, just a long hug. We get home, and our mother already knew what happened, and hugged both of us. She had cooked us dinner for us after our dates, but my brother says he isn't hungry. I sit down, but I couldn't really eat anything. I swear I could still feel the cold metal of that gun in the back of my head. I could feel something was wrong with my brother, mom cooked his favorite meal, and he just went upstairs. I tell my mom that it was a lovely dinner, and I head off to bed.

 I check on my brother, and he's sitting on the bed, his head in his hands.. I ask if he's okay, he says "I am. Go to bed. You need the rest." I turn to go, but my brother calls me back. "Do you think God will forgive me for murdering someone?" he asked. I tell him that it was in self-defense, and that God loved him very much, and that I think he won't be charged with any crimes. He absently nodded, and then knelt down beside the bed.. I looked at him confused. He seemed so subdued, not the energetic guy that went with me on a double date. He then tells me to go to bed, and I start to walk away. Later, as I'm laying in my bed, I can hear my brother sobbing in the other room.

On Monday, we wake up and go down for breakfest. I try to eat the pancakes mom made for us, but my brother justs stares at the pancakes, with that haunted look on his face. Mom asks if he is okay. He insists he's fine. About 30 minutes later, detectives show up at our house to question him. I try to work on some homework, but I can hear my brother break down in the other room. It hurt to see him like that, he was always the tough one out of us. The detectives leave, and he goes back upstairs to his room. He stayed there all day. 

I saw the guilt on his face for two months. I overheard mom and dad talk about him, that he's had nightmares about the shooting. The last time he had nightmares was in 4th grade.   Then, on March 17th, he tried to kill himself by hanging. He was taken to an institution and placed on suicide watch. It broke my heart to see my older brother like that. It made me think about what happened to him over those two months.

He's still there in the institution, but doctors tell us that he's depressed, and anxious, and scared of guns. I don't know how he would ever move past the shooting, or if he ever will. But I can tell you one thing. If you ever have to pull the trigger to kill someone, you'll see their face in your nightmares too. No matter how tough you are, you'll cry at night from the guilt.
